title: Consumption-plus-resilience pilot for private/on-prem packaging
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Run a closed pilot that validates a hybrid pricing model for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that combines a baseline license fee with consumption credits and optional resilience credits tied to SRE response SLAs. Goal is to increase conversion from PoC to committed contracts, reduce sticker shock for bursty workloads, and create a clear upgrade cadence for regulated customers.

Hypothesis: A two-part price (base license + usage credits) with an optional resilience SLA (paid monthly) will increase 12-month contract conversion by 20% relative to flat-seat or flat-node price models while preserving predictable baseline revenue for Redwood. Resilience credits (a modest recurring fee) buy prioritized support, reduced fallbacks, and guaranteed upgrade windows.

Proposed commercial structure (pilot):
- Base license: fixed monthly fee by deployment footprint (examples: $6,000/month per 4xA100-equivalent capacity block) — covers control plane, entitlement, minor security updates.
- Consumption credits: prepaid token credits sold in bands (e.g., 250k, 1M, 5M token buckets) with per-token overage rates. Customers draw from credits for burst traffic.
- Resilience (SLA) add-on: monthly charge (tiered: Standard Resilience, Enhanced Resilience, SRE-OnCall) that guarantees response times (4 hr, 1 hr, 30 min respectively) and includes a resilience credit pool that can be redeemed for rollbacks/patch prioritization.
- Upgrade cadence & obligations: security hotfixes pushed within 48 hours for customers on any resilience tier; critical patches auto-deployed if customer opts in; major feature upgrades scheduled quarterly with a 3-week opt-in testing window and a 60-day staged rollout for Enterprise. Non-opt-in customers receive advisory patches and a 6-month upgrade horizon.

Contract & product notes:
- Offer a 12-month pilot contract with breakpoints at 3 and 6 months to evaluate consumption patterns and allow adjust of credit bands.
- Include clear rollback and data migration language for on-prem upgrades.
- Add a clause where Redwood may recommend quantization/instance changes for cost-optimization; customers must approve before changes that affect model outputs.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Conversion rate from pilot to contracted customer >= 20% relative lift vs control cohort.
- Average ARR per customer in pilot cohort increases by >= 15% after 6 months.
- Reduction in support escalations (severity >= P1) by 25% for customers on resilience add-on.
- Upgrade opt-in compliance >= 80% for customers on Enhanced/Enterprise tiers.

Pilot candidates (early outreach):
- BankWave (regulated fintech) — interested in 1-year private VPC deployment, bursty trade analytics workload.
- MediSecure (healthcare SaaS) — needs strict upgrade windows and QSA-readiness.
- RetailEdge (large e-commerce) — peak seasonal bursts, interested in consumption credits.

Risks / trade-offs:
- Sales friction: added complexity may slow procurement. Mitigation: create templated SOWs and pricing sheets.
- Revenue forecasting: consumption makes short-term forecasting harder. Mitigation: require minimum prepaid credit bands and commit tiers.
- Engineering lift: automated safe-upgrade tooling and rollback hooks required for opt-in upgrades. Dependencies ENG-48760 (safe-upgrade framework) and ENG-49201 (automated rollback).

Next steps & timeline:
- Week 1: finalize pilot pricing bands and resilience SLA definitions (this ticket).
- Week 2: legal to draft pilot SOW + security questionnaire addendum.
- Week 3: sales/solutions collateral and quoting template.
- Week 4: identify pilot contracts and sign 2–3 pilot customers.
- Run pilot 90 days, measure metrics, then iterate.

Deliverables:
- Pricing matrix and quoting templates.
- SOW + sample contract language for pilot.
- Internal playbook for sales and solutions engineering.
- Dashboard to track pilot consumption, upgrade compliance, and escalations.

Requested reviews: Finance, Legal, Security, Solutions Engineering, Revenue Operations.
